'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Iran–Israel proxy conflict]]
**[[2024 Iran–Israel conflict]], [[Hezbollah–Israel conflict|Israel–Hezbollah conflict]]
***[[Majdal Shams attack]]
****Twelve people, all children, are killed in Iranian-manufactured [[Falaq-1]] rocket strikes on the [[Druze community in Israel|Druze]] village of [[Majdal Shams]] in the [[Israel]]i-occupied [[Golan Heights]]. Israel claims that [[Hezbollah]] is responsible for the attack, but Hezbollah denies any involvement. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/nine-people-killed-rocket-hits-football-pitch-israeli-occupied-golan-israel-2024-07-27/ (Reuters)]
***[[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] vows that Hezbollah will "pay a heavy price" which "it has not paid so far" in response to the attack. [https://www.barrons.com/news/israel-pm-says-hezbollah-to-pay-heavy-price-after-deadly-rocket-fire-12295f46 (''Barron's'')]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[2024 Ukrainian cyberattacks against Russia]]
***[[Hacker|Hackers]] from the [[Ministry of Defence (Ukraine)|Ministry of Defense of Ukraine]] escalate "massive" [[Cyberattack|cyberattacks]] on [[Russia]]'s largest banks, prohibiting any cash or credit transactions. Cyberattacks also target Russian [[Public transport|public transport systems]], [[Internet service provider|internet]] and [[Mobile network operator|mobile providers]], and [[Social networking service|social networks]]. [https://www.kyivpost.com/post/36471 (Kyiv Post)]
**[[Russia]]n forces capture the village of Lozovatske in [[Donetsk Oblast]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/russia-ukraine-war/russia-claims-capture-of-key-donetsk-settlement-lozovatskoye/3287025 (Anadolu Agency)]
*[[Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip]]
***More than fifty people, including fifteen children, are killed in [[Israel]]i attacks on a school used to shelter [[displaced people]] in [[Deir al-Balah]] in the [[Gaza Strip]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/7/27/israeli-attacks-kill-more-than-50-palestinians-across-gaza (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Mali War]]
**[[Battle of Tinzaouaten (2024)|Battle of Tinzaouaten]]
***[[Mali]]'s [[Tuareg]] coalition [[Permanent Strategic Framework for Peace, Security, and Development|CSP-PSD]] claimed to have killed and wounded dozens of [[Malian Armed Forces]] soldiers and [[Wagner Group]] mercenaries on the outskirts of [[Tinzaouaten]]. Russian sources said the head of the Wagner-affiliated Grey Zone [[Telegram channel]], which has 560,000 subscribers, died in the battle. The status of Wagner Group leader [[Anton Yelizarov]] is currently unknown. [https://www.golosameriki.com/a/v-mali-pogibli-rossijskie-naemniki-chvk-vagner-/7715902.html (VOA)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**At least 22 people are killed and 75 others are injured in a [[Rapid Support Forces]] attack on [[Al-Fashir]], [[North Darfur]], [[Sudan]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/least-22-killed-rsf-attacks-sudans-al-fashir-says-activist-group-2024-07-27/ (Reuters)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*The [[Ancient Rome|ancient Roman]] [[Appian Way]], the oldest [[Roman roads|Roman road]] which began construction in 312 B.C., is added to the [[UNESCO]] [[World Heritage Site|World Heritage List]]. [https://apnews.com/article/italy-rome-appian-way-unesco-world-heritage-list-35e308789b65127189bfd32b975dea23 (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents''' 
*Nine people are killed and others injured after a [[stampede]] during a concert at the [[Stade des Martyrs]] [[stadium]] in [[Kinshasa]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://apnews.com/article/congo-stampede-concert-kalambayi-53117d8c9ae72706c3daa67a1192da79 (AP)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c06km73rzzyo (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[Iran]] orders all government offices and commercial institutions to close tomorrow due to ongoing country-wide [[heat wave|heatwave]]s. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/heat-wave-forces-iran-shutter-government-offices-banks-112326729 (ABC)] [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-07-27/iran-to-shut-banks-offices-sunday-due-to-heat-state-tv-reports (Bloomberg)]

'''Law and crime'''
*Eight people are killed and five others are injured when a vehicle hits pedestrians in [[Changsha]], [[Hunan]], [[China]]. The perpetrator is arrested. [https://apnews.com/article/china-changsha-collision-pedestrians-killed-e1227eca206ce5f0284e0b6da62a2595 (AP)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2024 Summer Olympics]], [[Canada Soccer drone spying scandal]]
**In response to the spying incident involving the [[Canada women's national soccer team]] coaching staff using drones to spy on the [[New Zealand women's national football team|New Zealand team]], [[FIFA]] deducts six points from [[Canada]] in the [[Football at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's tournament|Paris Olympics women's football tournament]] and bans three coaches for one year, including head coach [[Bev Priestman]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2024/7/27/paris-2024-olympics-canada-women-football-soccer-priestman-drone-spying-scandal (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2024 UEFA Women's Under-19 Championship]]
**In [[association football]], [[Spain women's national under-19 football team|Spain]] defeats [[Netherlands women's national under-19 football team|the Netherlands]] 2–1 in the final to win their sixth [[UEFA Women's Under-19 Championship]] title. [https://www.uefa.com/womensunder19/news/028f-1b783de253b2-c1a95e0c979b-1000--uefa-women-s-under-19-euro-final-highlights-report-spain/ (UEFA)]
